YUTA.philosophy: Long-term ecosystem steward with a technical-economic philosophy centered on enabling Cardano to 'support the economic identities of billions of people.' YUTA balances optimism about Cardano's potential with a rigorous, conditions-based approach to approvals. Regularly discloses conflicts of interest and biases with unusual transparency. Highly active across all proposal categories. Bilingual Japanese-English rationales demonstrate engagement with both the Japanese community and the broader ecosystem.
YUTA.votingStyle: Conditional YES with detailed requirements. Frequently votes YES on major initiatives but attaches specific conditions that must be met before treasury withdrawals. Voted No on the Cardano Summit 2026 based on data-driven analysis of KPI failures. Known to vote on competing proposals simultaneously (e.g., both NCL proposals) to avoid governance failure.
YUTA.typicalRationale: Long, structured rationales with numbered points (5-12 per vote). Provides analytical breakdowns with data references (TapTools data, on-chain tx counts), conflict-of-interest disclosures, and conditional requirements for future governance actions. Regularly links to external Google Sheets tracking frameworks.
notableQuotes: Voted YES for the 7.5M and 275M budgets, including requirements that I would like met before treasury withdrawals could be made.

Treasury withdrawal governance actions must be performed in reasonably granular chunks. This is a requirement, and any unreasonably aggregated Treasury withdrawal governance actions will be immediately voted NO.
If voting YES: As an SPO, I have a conflict of interest here, as there is a possibility that my income will increase by supporting this proposal.
I was unable to identify a single transaction submission attributable to an enterprise (see adatool.net/tx-stats). 99% of usage is retail.

The 2025 proposal set a clear outcome metric: 15-20% year-on-year growth in developer numbers. That was the primary reason I voted YES at the time. It is to CF's credit that they have openly acknowledged this target was not met, but the problem lies beyond that acknowledgment.

InputEndorsers.philosophy: Philosophically anti-inflationary and deeply skeptical of large, bundled spending. Believes treasury funds should primarily support critical public goods rather than commercial ventures. Treats the ADA/USD rate as a first-order governance concern: approvals of large NCLs and budgets directly affect ADA's exchange value by creating sell pressure through fiat conversion. Advocates for gradual, deliberate parameter changes and phased budgets. Uniquely, self-discloses all potential conflicts of interest in detail, including indirect Catalyst involvement.
InputEndorsers.votingStyle: Frequently votes No on large spending even when supporting the general direction. Voted No on the 275M budget, No on the 350M NCL, No on the treasury tax decrease. Uses pragmatic abstentions when blocking would be counterproductive. Disclosed no financial conflicts when voting No, providing nuanced reasoning.
InputEndorsers.typicalRationale: Very long, discursive rationales with economic reasoning, numbered points, and substantial self-reflection. Cites market mechanisms and monetary theory (ADA as a financial system). Acknowledges counterarguments. Discloses conflicts in both YES and NO directions. References specific community contributors and on-chain data. Often the most analytical voice in any given proposal.
notableQuotes: In a still nascent blockchain economy, spending more essentially means converting the native token for fiat, and the result is devaluation. We are not exchanging ADA directly for Cardano economy goods and services, we are selling it into the real world.
My YES vote is a vote of trust in the Cardano community and its ability to wisely use constitutional tools.

If we are building a financial system, there is something to be said for financial predictability and gradual change. Outsiders looking at Cardano as an alternative financial system will look at how we manage change.

The problem I see with a very large first year NCL is that our budgetary and governance processes are the weakest, keep changing from week to week and are probably the most inefficient in the first year.
An umbrella proposal is too much of a mish-mash for me. [on Draper Dragon]

BWtake(長崎)Japan.philosophy: Philosophically ambitious and idealistic, framing Cardano governance within a broad worldview including 'butterfly effect' dynamics, liquid democracy as 'post-national democracy,' cypherpunk ideals, and even framing the constitution as 'DNA information' guiding AI in the Singularity era. Strong supporter of ecosystem funding and the Intersect budget process. Generally optimistic and supportive.
BWtake(長崎)Japan.votingStyle: Strong YES voter across most proposals. Supported the Constitution, tax decrease, 275M budget. Rationales are primarily in Japanese with some English. Often represents the Japanese Cardano community perspective.
BWtake(長崎)Japan.typicalRationale: Medium-to-long rationales, primarily in Japanese. Uses structured bullet points with numbered reasoning. Tends to frame votes in broad philosophical and societal terms. Both languages (EN/JP) used for many votes.
notableQuotes: シンギュラリティ時代のAIに対する「DNA情報」として技術発展が人類の利益に資する方向へ導き、中央集権型AIの暴走を防ぐ倫理的枠組みとして機能する可能性があります。 [The constitution may function as 'DNA information' guiding AI toward human benefit in the Singularity era, acting as an ethical framework preventing runaway centralized AI]

This 275M ADA budget proposal consolidates 39 individual proposals coordinated by Intersect and covers a wide range of domains including core development, governance, research, and marketing. I strongly support this comprehensive and balanced approach.

CardanoYoda (MANDA Pool).philosophy: Data-first governance philosophy with deep community engagement. CardanoYoda researches proposals extensively—citing exchange volume figures, on-chain tx data, polling results from community surveys, and direct conversations with proposers. Deeply concerned about governance standards and precedent-setting. Recognizes marketing as important but insists on sustainability and measurable ROI. Active pollster who surveys the community before major votes.
CardanoYoda (MANDA Pool).votingStyle: Votes No on proposals lacking data rigor or where the standards being set could be harmful to future governance. Voted No on both the Cardano Summit 2026 and the Snek loan despite acknowledging the value of the underlying ideas. Often provides conditional or multi-part reasoning.
CardanoYoda (MANDA Pool).typicalRationale: Very long, data-rich rationales with specific on-chain data points, polling results, and direct quotations from project teams. Links to PDF versions. Engages in community discourse before voting. Frequently the most empirically grounded analysis on any given proposal.
notableQuotes: Treasury loans cannot be based solely on 'trust me, bro.' That would set a dangerous precedent.
Cardano currently has high fees and slippage, making it less competitive than Solana or CEXs for swaps.
I am rejecting the proposal at this time to send a clear signal: Treasury loans must meet standards that will apply to all future projects.
We all have skin in the game. If we want to do spectacular events, we must first think about how to get Cardano back into the top 10.

Focusing on governance at Cardano Summit 2026 is not a good idea given the current problems with the centralization of voting power. Let's present governance to the world only when we ourselves are proud of it.

TriangleForces.philosophy: A self-described 'strategist' with decades in Technology, Media, and Telecommunications, TriangleForces applies a hard-nosed business and monetary philosophy to governance. Treats the treasury as a 'sovereign steward of scarce capital.' Consistently hostile to bundled proposals, vague KPIs, FOMO-driven spending, and what they call 'unchecked treasury spending' as 'the single greatest existential risk Cardano faces today.' Occasionally contradicts themselves—voting Yes on some large proposals (Critical Integrations) while railing against others.
TriangleForces.votingStyle: Default No voter with some strategic Yes votes (e.g., Critical Integrations Budget). Voted No on the 275M budget, both NCL proposals, Snek loan, Cardano Summit. Uses emphatic, often aggressive rhetoric. When voting Yes, positions it as 'bitter medicine' or strategic necessity.
TriangleForces.typicalRationale: Medium-length, high-rhetoric rationales with frequent use of bold text and emphatic declarations. Invokes business experience, monetary theory ('disinflationary emission schedule'), and compares to Bitcoin's supply model. Tends to lecture the community on fiscal discipline. Occasionally inconsistent—votes Yes on 70M Critical Integrations while criticizing others for lesser amounts.
notableQuotes: Unchecked treasury spending is the single greatest existential risk Cardano faces today.
Treasury money is not marketing pocket money, and prestige is not a public good!
This proposal reeks of kindergarten-level thinking: shouting loudest in the biggest room instead of whispering strategically in the right ears.
We cannot govern a ghost town. [justifying Yes on Critical Integrations]
The Treasury must behave like a sovereign steward of scarce capital, not a venture lender without collateral, enforceable covenants, or credible cash-flow evidence.
It stings to fund 'basics' from the treasury at this maturity stage of the chain.
I just regret that the majority of DReps have wasted 50 million ADA on an unsecured loan for a meme coin.

$brock.philosophy: Concise libertarian-leaning fiscal conservative. Believes the treasury is accumulating too much ADA (prefers ~1% of circulating supply vs current ~4%). Prioritizes fiscal responsibility, decentralized lending (DeFi should provide loans, not the treasury), and building real value before marketing. Dislikes 'grey area' in constitutional language. Occasionally changes position when given sufficient structural guarantees (e.g., Draper Dragon Yes).
$brock.votingStyle: Short, decisive No votes on spending proposals with terse rationales. Voted No on 275M budget, Cardano Summit 2026, Snek loan, Cardano Constitution. Voted Yes on tax decrease. Sometimes provides surprise Yes when structural safeguards satisfy concerns.
$brock.typicalRationale: Very short rationales (1-3 sentences to 2 paragraphs). Gets to the point immediately. No rhetorical flourish. References specific data when used (ADA price at Summit, treasury % of supply). Sometimes blunt to the point of being dismissive.
notableQuotes: A technology-based constitution should not be left up to subjective interpretation of what is 'reasonable'. It should be black and white.
The treasury will soon hold 4% of ADA's circulating supply, which is too high. Somewhere around 1% would make a lot more sense.

ADA's value was $0.90 on the day of last year's Cardano Summit, and has only gone down since the event, sitting at $0.25 today. This is the time to put our heads down and build what the future needs, not get together and party.
This budget is massively beyond both the NCL I voted for as well as the sum of all budget items I voted for, therefore I cannot vote yes.
Cardano's DeFi sector features many well-built products, with multiple lending platforms included in that list. If a project needs a loan they should be using the appropriate products.

SASA_nagamaru_ながまる.philosophy: Process-integrity focused. Believes NCL must be set before proposals are evaluated. Concerned about governance legitimacy and the proper sequencing of budget decisions. Frequently bilingual (Japanese/English). Often abstains when strategically aligned with direction but concerned about specifics. Thoughtful about the difference between supporting a direction vs. approving a specific proposal.
SASA_nagamaru_ながまる.votingStyle: Voted No on 275M budget due to process concerns. Abstained on Cardano Summit (acknowledging strategic merit but insufficient ROI clarity). Tends to evaluate both substance and procedural legitimacy.
SASA_nagamaru_ながまる.typicalRationale: Medium-length bilingual rationales (Japanese/English). Structured with clear logic. Focuses on process integrity and proper governance sequencing. Sometimes uses abstain strategically when uncertain.
notableQuotes: During the Voltaire era, it's not just about what we fund—but how we fund it. A clear, disciplined process will build long-term trust and stability for Cardano.
I firmly believe that we should define the NCL first—before evaluating proposals.
I do not have sufficient confidence in the return on investment, particularly regarding how event-driven exposure will translate into measurable on-chain activity.

jonahkoch.philosophy: Pragmatic ecosystem accelerationist. Strongly supports institutional infrastructure and professional capital management for Cardano. Believes governance should enable action rather than obstruct it—but demands structural safeguards when doing so. Highly engaged with financial details of proposals, reading fund structures, waterfall mechanics, and VC terms carefully. Notable for voting Yes on Draper Dragon with one of the most detailed rationales in the dataset.
jonahkoch.votingStyle: Generally votes Yes on significant ecosystem investments when structural safeguards are present. Voted Yes on 275M budget (urgency argument), Yes on Draper Dragon, Yes on Snek loan, Yes on Critical Integrations. Abstained on bundled Summit proposal (and would evaluate the split versions). Voted No on Cardano Budget Process Framework.
jonahkoch.typicalRationale: Very long, highly structured rationales with detailed financial analysis. Uniquely willing to read and cite waterfall structures, fund mechanics, management fee details, and Draper network specifics. References specific portfolio companies and program alumni. Among the most technically sophisticated financial analyses in governance.
notableQuotes: This 70M ADA is more than a budget request, it functions as a bond of accountability. The founding entities are now publicly and collectively tied to delivering measurable outcomes.
This is the first serious attempt to deploy treasury capital as structured investment rather than grants or operational budgets.
The economic alignment strongly favors the ecosystem. Roughly 90% of Tranche One funds deploy directly into ecosystem support.
At minimum, participating stake thresholds should use live voting stake, bundling should be eliminated in favor of individual proposal submissions. [voting No on Budget Process Framework]
This is a loan, not a handout. 5 million ADA at 2.44% interest, repaid within five years from Snek's product revenues.

Kostas Panagias.philosophy: Methodical, evidence-seeking governance participant who explicitly reads other DReps' rationales before forming opinions ('I read other people's rationales because no one knows everything'). Believes liquid democracy makes imperfect constitutions acceptable. Tracks his own voting record to assess budget alignment. Values broad community representation and spirit-of-the-law over letter-of-the-law interpretation.
Kostas Panagias.votingStyle: Supportive Yes voter aligned with community consensus while applying careful individual judgment. Voted Yes on 275M budget (citing 38/39 personal votes matched). Voted No on Cardano Summit (bundling concern). Consistent and principled in recorded positions.
Kostas Panagias.typicalRationale: Structured, medium-to-long rationales with numbered sections. Explains reasoning step by step. Notable for citing his own voting record as evidence of alignment. Acknowledges concerns while explaining why they don't block support.
notableQuotes: I read other people's rationales because no one knows everything, and I might be missing important context or an interesting viewpoint.
Perfect is the enemy of good. We operate in a liquid democracy where it is easy to make changes when necessary.

Out of the 39 proposals, I have voted YES on the vast majority, with only 4 NO votes and 4 ABSTAINS. This strong alignment gives me confidence that this budget represents both my own judgment and the broader community's priorities.
People from third-world countries often have very low voting power and are vastly underrepresented in governance processes.

SIPO.philosophy: Institutionally sophisticated DRep from Japan (tokyo.sipo.io domain) that approaches governance with a comparative ecosystem lens. Regularly compares Cardano's governance processes to Polkadot OpenGov and Cosmos treasury systems. Highly engaged with process design, Ekklesia mechanics, and DRep workload. Bilingual Japanese-English. Supports structured frameworks but flags specific implementation risks (e.g., Ekklesia counting methodology).
SIPO.votingStyle: Generally Yes on frameworks and ecosystem proposals. Voted Yes on Budget Process Framework with detailed conditional expectations. Consistently supports institutional evolution. Tends to combine support with a list of concrete expectations for implementation.
SIPO.typicalRationale: Very long, bilingual, exhaustively structured rationales with numbered sections in both Japanese and English. Cites comparative blockchain governance (Polkadot, Cosmos). Provides specific expectations and monitoring requests. Among the most institutionally sophisticated rationales in the dataset.
notableQuotes: Compared to Polkadot OpenGov facing treasury sustainability concerns and Cosmos still transitioning from simple community pool spending, Cardano's multi-role governance (DRep + SPO + CC) combined with smart-contract-enforced milestone disbursements represents one of the most mature treasury governance frameworks in the industry.
SIPO experienced firsthand the challenges of reviewing 194 proposals in inconsistent formats.
A visible roadmap toward reducing single-entity dependency in future cycles. [expectation for Intersect]

Cardano Foundation.philosophy: Institutional pragmatist with high standards for evidence and process. The CF positions itself as a responsible steward of governance norms. Votes pragmatically—supporting imperfect proposals when delays would be worse—while consistently demanding financial modeling, multi-scenario projections, transparency, and reform. Unusually, discloses conflicts of interest (e.g., CEO on Snek advisory board, operational involvement in Draper Dragon). Advocates for 'purpose-led' rather than 'vendor-led' budget processes.
Cardano Foundation.votingStyle: Mix of strategic Yes and principled No. Voted Yes on Constitution, Yes on 275M budget (with extensive caveats), No on treasury tax decrease (lack of modeling), Yes on Draper Dragon (with conflict disclosure), Abstain on Summit (deferred to revised proposal), Yes on Snek loan. Always provides detailed rationales. Signals what future votes will require.
Cardano Foundation.typicalRationale: Extremely long, professionally written rationales (often 1000+ words). Formatted with bold headers, bullet points, and PDF versions linked. Cites specific documents (Economic Parameters whitepaper), demands multi-year projections, scenario modeling, Edinburgh Decentralization Index. Among the most rigorous standards setters.
notableQuotes: Our yes vote is a pragmatic decision to ensure that: the crucial step of establishing a budget is taken, funding for 2025 can be received, and to demonstrate progress in on-chain governance - despite our significant reservations about the budget process.
We advocate that the 2026 process shifts from the current 'vendor-led' model to a more effective 'purpose-led' approach.
A revised proposal should include: Multi-year Treasury Projections, Staking Simulations, Inflation Analysis, and a Reversion/Recovery Plan.
This proposal introduces an innovative and necessary funding mechanism for the Cardano ecosystem: a treasury-backed loan for a scaling commercial entity.
We worked closely with the Draper Dragon team to orchestrate the setup of Arouet Holdings and serve as the constitutional administrator. Despite our operational involvement, we are voting YES.

EMURGO.philosophy: Institutional DRep that consistently supports governance framework evolution and ecosystem development. Votes based on constitutional compliance, governance process milestones, and ecosystem growth potential. Less analytically detailed than Cardano Foundation but reliably aligned with major institutional actions. Views this as 'upholding the governance framework.' Acknowledges uncertainty without blocking progress.
EMURGO.votingStyle: Consistent Yes voter on major institutional actions (Constitution, 275M budget, Draper Dragon, Snek loan). Rationales are shorter and more deferential to process than CF. Rarely votes No.
EMURGO.typicalRationale: Medium-length rationales with clear structure but less analytical depth than Cardano Foundation. Uses a 'Summary/Rationale/Conclusion' format. Cites constitutional compliance, oversight mechanisms, and community process participation.
notableQuotes: This budget info action represents a constitutionally required checkpoint under Cardano Constitution, and its passage is a prerequisite for any treasury withdrawal.
By introducing a loan-based model, it sets a precedent for how Treasury funds can be used responsibly while ensuring capital can be recycled back into the ecosystem.
Approving the first tranche is a reasonable way to test this model while preserving future governance oversight.

Cerkoryn.philosophy: Evidence-based, historically grounded governance participant. Frequently cites historical context (tau was recommended at 5% by IOG researchers, changed to 20% at launch). Believes the first budget cycle should be modest to refine procedures. Maintains an active GitHub governance reference repository. Reads DRep discussions and constitutional draft history. Generally prefers iterative improvement to bold first actions.
Cerkoryn.votingStyle: Mixed—voted Yes on Constitution, Yes on tax decrease (despite preferring gradual change), No on 275M budget (too large/bundled), No on Summit 2026 (poor ROI), Yes on Draper Dragon (treasury-first waterfall was 'saving grace'). Willing to change position when specific safeguards satisfy concerns.
Cerkoryn.typicalRationale: Medium-length rationales with historical context and clear reasoning. Links to GitHub repository. Acknowledges specific reservations while explaining whether they're deal-breakers. Honest about uncertainty.
notableQuotes: IOG researchers initially recommended setting the Tau parameter at 5%, but prior to the launch of the Shelley mainnet, it was changed to 20%. Additionally, due to the way block rewards are calculated, the effective tax rate is actually 33%.
A more modest budget with fewer proposals would allow us to refine our procedures and iteratively improve for the next cycle.
The decision to pay back the treasury FIRST before the GP makes any profit is the saving grace to this proposal. [on Draper Dragon]

Rudianos.philosophy: Pragmatic community-oriented DRep who sees governance as evolutionary. Values concrete utility and measurable outcomes. For budget proposals, distinguishes between approving a budget (enabling a process) vs. approving individual withdrawals. For marketing, insists on a comprehensive strategy rather than ad-hoc proposals. Relatively concise in expression.
Rudianos.votingStyle: Supportive Yes on major ecosystem actions (Constitution, 275M budget) with clear caveats. Voted No on Summit (no marketing framework in place). Balances ecosystem support with fiscal discipline.
Rudianos.typicalRationale: Short-to-medium rationales. Gets to the point. Acknowledges nuance without excessive detail. Distinguishes between supporting a direction and supporting specific execution.
notableQuotes: This is a good and necessary first step to governance and provides what it sets out to provide; a foundational pillar for minimum viable governance.

Treating marketing initiatives as ad-hoc, standalone proposals is inefficient. We should have a comprehensive strategy that outlines our total marketing spend and community priorities before approving individual, fragmented requests.

Kostas_Panagias.philosophy: See 'Kostas Panagias' entry above (same DRep, note deduplication).

AdaStat.philosophy: Operator of the AdaStat.net blockchain explorer. Pragmatic and minimal in governance—prefers to let process flow when constitutional guardrails are adequate. Considers some governance steps 'mostly adds delays and confusion' when the final vote threshold is already high. Concise.
AdaStat.votingStyle: Generally votes Yes with brief rationales. Not a significant blocker. Focuses on enabling the process.
AdaStat.typicalRationale: Very short rationales (1-2 sentences to short paragraph). Direct, businesslike. No rhetorical flourish.
notableQuotes: I think this step mostly adds delays and confusion, since 67% is already needed in the final vote. But since it's part of the process now, I'm voting Yes to let projects move forward.
Despite the fact that this Cardano Constitution is still far from perfect, it is definitely sufficient to move forward.

HOSKY.philosophy: One of the most evolved DReps in the dataset—the 'HOSKY' meme token persona applies a surprisingly rigorous governance framework called 'Cardano First' with five pillars: Adoption, Economic Sustainability, Governance Transparency, Decentralization, and Scalability. Shows substantial growth from simple Yes/Abstain to detailed, multi-layered analyses. Particularly sharp on event accountability and the tension between institutional entity self-funding vs. treasury dependency. Maintains PDF-linked rationales.
HOSKY.votingStyle: Evolved from simple Yes/Abstain to nuanced mixed voting. Voted Yes on Constitution, Abstained on 275M budget (structural concerns), No on Summit 2026 (CF sustainability commitment broken), Yes on Draper Dragon (detailed 5-pillar analysis), Yes on Snek loan (procedural Yes with withdrawal conditions).
HOSKY.typicalRationale: Later rationales are very long, structured with bold headers matching the 5 Cardano First pillars. Links to PDF versions. Acknowledges risks explicitly and lists them. Earlier rationales were shorter and simpler—significant evolution over time.
notableQuotes: The treasury is not a savings account - it's a growth engine.

The Cardano Foundation committed to making this sustainable, and one year later it's back asking for the same money. No until the Cardano Foundation demonstrates a credible path to event self-funding.
A core principle of crypto is don't trust, verify. Relying on trust alone is not a good precedent.
The treasury is not an events slush fund.
This is the largest single treasury withdrawal I've voted on, so I want to be explicit about why it clears every pillar of the Cardano First framework.

Wada DRep.philosophy: Represents a decentralized network of community builders across Africa and diaspora. Frames governance through inclusivity, community empowerment, and Africa's representation in blockchain governance. Supported the Constitution as a culmination of grassroots workshops and translation services they personally ran. Strong supporter of Intersect-led budget processes when aligned with community-vetted proposals. One of the most explicitly pan-African voices in governance.
Wada DRep.votingStyle: Strong Yes voter on inclusive, community-validated proposals. Voted Yes on Constitution (as direct result of their organizing work), Yes on 275M budget (community validation process honored). Rationales are eloquent and emphasize representation.
Wada DRep.typicalRationale: Long, eloquent rationales with narrative framing of community work done. References internal deliberative frameworks and 'treasury ceiling' of their own organization. Advocacy-oriented but thoughtful.
notableQuotes: From hosting educational workshops to ensure that community members understand governance principles, to facilitating town hall discussions where diverse voices could contribute to shaping the constitution, we have consistently championed inclusive decision-making.
This proposal represents the most coordinated and participatory budget process in Cardano's history and deserves our support as a model for future funding cycles.
A robust ecosystem must be built on inclusion, legitimacy, and capacity, not on legacy position alone.

William Doyle.philosophy: Philosophical and community-centered. Frames Cardano governance as an intergenerational project ('hand it down to our children'). References classical literature (Ulysses pact). Pragmatic on budget decisions—votes Yes on important proposals despite reservations about process. Advocates for tooling to enable crowd-sourced governance action deposits. Maintains a public GitHub repository of vote contexts.
William Doyle.votingStyle: Yes voter who acknowledges tensions but prioritizes momentum. Voted Yes on Constitution (poetic rationale), Yes on 275M budget (despite omnibus concerns). Pragmatic while principled.
William Doyle.typicalRationale: Short-to-medium, often poetic rationales for big votes. Pragmatic and brief for procedural votes. Links to GitHub for detail.
notableQuotes: This constitution, the product of many conversations from around the world, enshrines our values and shall act as our Ulysses pact to constrain us in times of temptation. May we forever remember what came before, the mistakes that were made, and the lessons that were learned.
Now that Cardano belongs to us, it is our duty to preserve it, enhance it, and, when the time comes, hand it down to our children.
Next year we should try to avoid an omnibus budget. To make this feasible, we will need to build an effective tool to enable governance action deposits to be crowd sourced.

GAIA.philosophy: Technical governance idealist concerned about on-chain enforceability, plutocracy risk, and financial barriers to participation. Applies a personal NCL of 250M ADA and votes accordingly. Critical of 1-lovelace-1-vote model, advocates for DIDs and quadratic voting. Raises concrete constitutional concerns (govDeposit at 100k ADA is too high, depleting governance access). Engages with governance tooling bugs directly.
GAIA.votingStyle: Voted Yes on Constitution (pragmatic, with detailed improvement wishlist). Voted No on 275M budget (exceeds personal NCL, against omnibus). Personal NCL standard is rigorously applied.
GAIA.typicalRationale: Medium-to-long rationales with specific constitutional article citations and technical governance critique. Lists concrete action items for improvement.
notableQuotes: The 1-lovelace-1-vote model sadly leads to centralized oligarchy or plutocracy, and we are in this situation right from the start of governance.

DRep and Direct Voter registration fees should be lowered significantly so that meaningful participation can happen. Finances alone are not an adequate determining factor for leadership or governance capabilities of a person.

A significant amount of proposals that were successfully passed did not meet the on chain threshold of 2.69B ADA. Omnibus budgets are the only way skewed results like this are able to circumvent intended On-Chain guardrails.
There is currently no way for a competing Cardano Constitution to be submitted in time on gov.tools — a deliberate choice that was made.

Eternl DRep Committee.philosophy: Committee-based DRep representing the Eternl wallet team. Consistently pragmatic and process-enabling. Views most budget and framework actions as 'pro forma' steps within the constitutional process rather than consequential decisions in themselves. Short, technically clear rationales. Maintains a GitHub repository for transparency.
Eternl DRep Committee.votingStyle: Nearly always Yes. Views Info Actions and budget steps as enabling future granular votes rather than direct spending decisions. Very rarely blocks.
Eternl DRep Committee.typicalRationale: Short, clear, TL;DR format. Focused on the mechanics of the governance action rather than the substance of proposals. Provides GitHub links for transparency.
notableQuotes: Proposals on the list of this budget info action can POTENTIALLY get funding. If individual withdrawal actions are submitted, the threshold for each proposal to actually get funds will be 67%. That's restrictive enough, and this budget info action is just pro forma to further the budget process as per the Constitution.
This marks the beginning of decentralized decision-making, ensuring adaptability and accountability. It is a prerequisite for Cardano's development in 2025 and beyond.

hix_coffeepool.philosophy: ADA value-preservation focused. Core concern: 'For any currency, supply control is far more critical than technological advancement.' Believes large treasury withdrawals directly damage ADA value and harm all holders. Applies a conservative fiscal lens to all proposals.
hix_coffeepool.votingStyle: Voted Yes on Constitution (pragmatic), No on 275M budget (supply control concerns). Generally conservative on spending.
hix_coffeepool.typicalRationale: Medium-length rationales with a monetary philosophy emphasis. Clear and direct.
notableQuotes: For any currency, supply control is far more critical than technological advancement. A currency must preserve value and maintain trust in transactions.
Large-scale ADA withdrawals from the treasury could significantly harm the value of ADA, potentially undermining the entire Cardano ecosystem.

CaFi.philosophy: Minimal rationale DRep. Fully aligned with Intersect processes. Short, decisive yes votes.
CaFi.votingStyle: Very short Yes votes. 'There should be no further delay. We fully support Intersect.'
CaFi.typicalRationale: 1-2 sentences. One of the shortest rationale writers in the dataset.
notableQuotes: There should be no further delay. We fully support Intersect.

Dave.philosophy: Decentralization purist. Primary concern: off-chain voting processes 'lack transparency, auditability, and decentralization.' Rejects bundled proposals and relies exclusively on on-chain verifiable data. Critical of unverifiable off-chain participation metrics cited in proposals.
Dave.votingStyle: Voted No on 275M budget (off-chain voting concerns, bundling, unverifiable metrics).
Dave.typicalRationale: Medium-length, focused on governance process integrity and on-chain verifiability.
notableQuotes: The proposal relies on unverifiable off-chain metrics, such as the claim that 'More than 3.8B ada in voting stake participated.' Without on-chain data, such figures cannot be independently verified or trusted.
As a DRep, I cannot support off-chain processes that lack transparency, auditability, and decentralization.

Nimuë Lady of the Lake Pool.philosophy: Technically focused governance participant with specific constitutional improvement proposals. Voted Yes on Constitution while noting concrete missing elements (public/permissionless statement, definitions, hard fork ecosystem readiness).
Nimuë Lady of the Lake Pool.typicalRationale: Short-to-medium rationales with specific technical/constitutional observations. Practical and direct.
notableQuotes: The tenets should explicitly state that Cardano is public and permissionless, ideally as the first one.
A guardrail for hard forks should ensure the ecosystem (exchanges, dApps) is ready without strict thresholds like stake pools.

AlignedYes.description: DReps who support most major proposals with short, process-enabling rationales. Rarely block. View info actions as procedural steps.
characteristics: Often acknowledge reservations but don't let them block

SkepticalCritical.description: DReps who apply genuine scrutiny, often vote No, but are persuadable by specific safeguards. Not dogmatically opposed to spending.
members: Nimuë Lady of the Lake Pool
characteristics: Long rationales with specific concerns listed
Will vote Yes if structural safeguards are added

PrincipledNo.description: DReps with consistent opposition based on stated principles (fiscal conservatism, decentralization, anti-bundling). Hard to persuade.

ProcessFocused.description: DReps who prioritize governance process integrity, constitutional compliance, and proper sequencing above substantive agreement.
characteristics: Often conditional Yes votes with requirements
Vote No when process is wrong even if content is good
Demand proper NCL → budget → withdrawal sequencing

Technical.description: DReps who focus on technical merit, on-chain data, and empirical evidence. Cite specific metrics.
members: Nimuë Lady of the Lake Pool

EconomicFinancial.description: DReps who prioritize financial prudence, ADA value preservation, and treasury sustainability above other concerns.
characteristics: Prefer lower NCLs and spending ceilings
Concern about sell pressure from treasury withdrawals

InstitutionalRepresentative.description: DReps representing major organizations with governance responsibilities and disclosures.

highQuality.description: DReps who write thorough, well-reasoned rationales with specific data, referenced sources, and transparent reasoning
characteristics: PDF versions linked for long rationales

mediumQuality.description: DReps who write clear, honest rationales with adequate reasoning but less analytical depth
members: Nimuë Lady of the Lake Pool

lowQuality.description: DReps who write minimal or one-liner rationales without substantive reasoning
members: CardanoYoda (links to external file without inline text)
characteristics: Some just link to external documents without inline summary

constitutionCiters.description: DReps who explicitly quote or reference the Cardano Constitution in rationales

dataReferencing.description: DReps who cite specific on-chain data, TapTools statistics, or external research
members: CardanoYoda (exchange volumes, DEX data, polling results)

copyPasteRationales.notes: No clear copy-paste rationales identified. However, several DReps (YUTA, SIPO, BWtake) use near-identical content in both Japanese and English sections of the same rationale (bilingual versions of the same text), which is expected and legitimate. No cases of different DReps sharing identical text were identified in the sampled proposals.

japaneseLanguage.description: Several high-activity DReps write rationales in Japanese (often bilingual). The Japanese Cardano community is well-represented and sophisticated.
drepList: hix_coffeepool (primarily English but Japanese community context)
japaneseLanguage.notes: The Japanese DRep community is notably active, well-organized, and produces some of the highest-quality rationales. YUTA and SIPO in particular are among the most rigorous governance participants overall. Japanese rationales often provide both languages for accessibility.

africanRepresentation.description: Wada DRep explicitly represents the African community and diaspora. Kostas Panagias notes Africa has less than 2% representation.
africanRepresentation.notes: The governance gap for Africa is acknowledged by multiple DReps. Wada explicitly does translation work and community organizing across the continent.

vietnameseLanguage.notes: Vietnamese community present but limited in sampled data.

latinAmericanRepresentation.notes: Latin American representation present in proposal listings but not deeply sampled.

english.description: Majority of DReps write in English regardless of origin. Clear dominant governance language.
english.notes: Most DReps from Europe, Americas, and Oceania write exclusively in English. Some non-native speakers write in English anyway, with varying quality.

distinctiveFeatures: Explicit conflict-of-interest disclosures (CEO on advisory boards)
Demands rigorous economic modeling before supporting parameter changes
Advocates for 2026 process reform ('purpose-led vs vendor-led')
cardanoFoundation.keyDifference: Unlike individual DReps, CF must balance governance norms with ecosystem leadership role. Occasionally caught in conflicts of interest (Draper Dragon involvement) which it discloses.

distinctiveFeatures: Shorter rationales than CF but same institutional positioning
Generally supportive of major ecosystem actions
Less analytical depth, more deferential to CF on complex issues
emurgo.keyDifference: EMURGO's governance voice is less developed than CF's. Votes similarly on most major issues but with less analytical elaboration.

distinctiveFeatures: Views most Info Actions as procedural 'pro forma' steps
eternlDRepCommittee.keyDifference: Unlike founding entities, Eternl represents a specific product team with commercial interests. Governance participation seems primarily aimed at enabling ecosystem operations.

distinctiveFeatures: Long, narrative rationales about community work
wadaDRep.keyDifference: Wada functions as a community aggregator DRep, representing many delegators across a geographic community rather than a product or founding organization.

distinctiveFeatures: Counter-intuitive: meme persona applying rigorous governance framework
Significant evolution from simple votes to highly detailed analyses
Will vote No on major institutional proposals (Summit)
Sharp accountability focus on institutional entities
hosky.keyDifference: HOSKY is the most striking example of governance persona evolution. Demonstrates that even a meme identity can develop into a serious governance participant with clear frameworks. Contrarian to large institutional asks.

hosky.evolutionDescription: The most notable evolution in the dataset. Early HOSKY votes were simple Yes/Abstain with basic rationales. By the Draper Dragon and Summit 2026 votes, HOSKY had developed a comprehensive 'Cardano First' framework with 5 named pillars and PDF-linked detailed analyses running hundreds of words. The Summit No vote with detailed accountability critique represents a fundamentally different level of governance engagement than early votes.
hosky.directionOfChange: From simple process-enabler to rigorous accountability watchdog

inputEndorsers.evolutionDescription: Consistently high-quality throughout the dataset, but shows a pragmatic evolution: voted No on the 275M budget but then actively abstained on the DeFi Withdrawal (rather than blocking) when acknowledging the proposer's unique credentials. Shows growing sophistication about when a 'No' is warranted vs. when a 'blocking abstain' misuses the governance mechanism.
inputEndorsers.directionOfChange: Consistent high quality; more nuanced use of abstain vs No over time

triangleForces.evolutionDescription: Shows notable inconsistency rather than evolution: applies strong fiscal conservatism across most proposals while voting Yes on the 70M Critical Integrations Budget (one of the largest single proposals) with rhetoric about 'bitter medicine' and 'entry ticket to global markets.' The contrast with No votes on 5M Snek and 14M Summit reveals a strategic rather than principled fiscal stance.
triangleForces.directionOfChange: Revealed inconsistency: fiscal principle is selectively applied based on strategic value judgments

yuta.evolutionDescription: YUTA's rationale sophistication increases with proposal complexity. The Cardano Summit 2026 No vote is the most developed analysis—running thousands of words with firsthand observations from TEAMZ events, data on on-chain enterprise activity, and systematic interrogation of marketing KPI methodology. Earlier votes were shorter. YUTA also increasingly adds disclosure of conflicts and bias.
yuta.directionOfChange: Growing analytical depth, especially on marketing/events where YUTA has direct Japanese community experience

notableQuotes.quote: This constitution, the product of many conversations from around the world, enshrines our values and shall act as our Ulysses pact to constrain us in times of temptation. May we forever remember what came before, the mistakes that were made, and the lessons that were learned. Now that Cardano belongs to us, it is our duty to preserve it, enhance it, and, when the time comes, hand it down to our children.
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Constitution to Replace the Interim Constitution
notableQuotes.significance: The most eloquent rationale in the entire dataset. Frames governance as intergenerational responsibility.

notableQuotes.quote: In a still nascent blockchain economy, spending more essentially means converting the native token for fiat, and the result is devaluation. We are not exchanging ADA directly for Cardano economy goods and services, we are selling it into the real world. The ADA is not recycled internally.
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Blockchain Ecosystem Budget - 275M ada Administered by Intersect
notableQuotes.significance: Clearest articulation of the ADA sell-pressure mechanism that distinguishes blockchain treasury economics from traditional fiscal spending.

notableQuotes.quote: Treasury money is not marketing pocket money, and prestige is not a public good!
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Summit 2026 and TOKEN2049 Singapore
notableQuotes.significance: Memorable one-liner encapsulating the core fiscal conservatism argument against events spending.

notableQuotes.quote: This proposal reeks of kindergarten-level thinking: shouting loudest in the biggest room instead of whispering strategically in the right ears.
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Summit 2026 and TOKEN2049 Singapore

notableQuotes.quote: We cannot govern a ghost town.

notableQuotes.quote: The 2025 proposal set a clear outcome metric: 15-20% year-on-year growth in developer numbers. That was the primary reason I voted YES at the time... the number of cases that concretely demonstrate the 2025 goal of 'acquiring and retaining new developers' is effectively zero.
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Summit 2026 and TOKEN2049 Singapore
notableQuotes.significance: Demonstrates accountability-based governance: changing vote when stated KPIs from prior year were not delivered.

notableQuotes.quote: In epoch 622, I was unable to identify a single transaction submission attributable to an enterprise (see adatool.net/tx-stats). 99% of usage is retail.

notableQuotes.significance: Rare empirical claim backed by on-chain data directly contradicting the Summit's enterprise adoption narrative.

notableQuotes.quote: If we are building a financial system, there is something to be said for financial predictability and gradual change. Outsiders looking at Cardano as an alternative financial system will look at how we manage change.

notableQuotes.quote: I read other people's rationales because no one knows everything, and I might be missing important context or an interesting viewpoint. I always try to broaden my perspectives and listen not only to those with whom I agree but, more importantly, to those with whom I disagree.
notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Constitution to Replace the Interim Constitution

notableQuotes.quote: The 1-lovelace-1-vote model sadly leads to centralized oligarchy or plutocracy, and we are in this situation right from the start of governance, which was predetermined for CIP 1694.

notableQuotes.proposal: Cardano Blockchain Ecosystem Budget - 275M ada Administered by Intersect

notableQuotes.quote: シンギュラリティ時代のAIに対する「DNA情報」として技術発展が人類の利益に資する方向へ導き、中央集権型AIの暴走を防ぐ倫理的枠組みとして機能する可能性があります。 [The constitution may function as 'DNA information' guiding AI toward human benefit in the Singularity era, acting as an ethical framework preventing the runaway of centralized AI]

insights.finding: Rationale quality is highly bimodal. A small cohort (YUTA, InputEndorsers, jonahkoch, Cardano Foundation, CardanoYoda, SIPO, HOSKY) writes substantive, data-referenced analyses. A larger tail writes process-enabling 1-3 sentence rationales. This bifurcation means the intellectual work of governance is concentrated in fewer than 10 DReps even though voting power is more distributed.

The Japanese DRep community (YUTA, SIPO, BWtake, SASA, AKYO) is disproportionately active, well-organized, and analytically sophisticated relative to their numerical representation. YUTA and SIPO produce some of the most rigorous governance rationales in the dataset. YUTA explicitly attends events like TEAMZ and reports firsthand observations in governance rationales.

A significant minority of DReps (InputEndorsers, $brock, TriangleForces, hix_coffeepool) treat ADA token value preservation as a first-order governance consideration, arguing that treasury withdrawals create direct sell pressure through fiat conversion. This is a coherent but minority position—most DReps focus on ecosystem value creation rather than token price.

The most robust accountability challenges to the Cardano Foundation and EMURGO come not from 'No' voting skeptics but from HOSKY and CardanoYoda—unexpected sources. HOSKY's Summit rejection was sharper and better-documented than most institutional analyses. The meme persona as accountability watchdog is a notable governance phenomenon.

The 275M budget vote revealed deep community ambivalence about bundled proposals. At least 6 DReps who voted Yes did so while explicitly criticizing the bundling (Rudianos, William Doyle, jonahkoch, Cardano Foundation, YUTA). Several No voters (InputEndorsers, $brock, TriangleForces) cited bundling as the primary objection. This near-universal criticism of bundling from both Yes and No voters suggests strong consensus for individual proposal submissions in 2026.

Multiple DReps (SASA, GAIA, YUTA, InputEndorsers) criticized the 2025 budget process for improper sequencing: NCL should be set before proposals, which should be granular before a budget is assembled. The fact that the 275M budget passed despite this widespread process criticism suggests that urgency and momentum concerns outweigh process purity concerns in aggregate DRep behavior.

YUTA sets an unusually high standard by disclosing conflicts of interest in both directions (SPO income if Yes, Intersect committee role if No) and explaining why neither amounts to recusal-level conflict. Cardano Foundation also discloses CEO board memberships. This transparency norm is not universal—most DReps do not disclose potential conflicts even when they exist (e.g., SPOs voting on treasury tax decreases).

The Draper Dragon proposal introduced a new concept to Cardano governance: the treasury as structured investment capital rather than grants or operational budgets. The majority of high-quality DReps supported it (YUTA, jonahkoch, HOSKY, Cardano Foundation, Cerkoryn, $brock) while high-quality skeptics (InputEndorsers, TriangleForces) opposed it. This debate marks a maturation inflection point in Cardano treasury philosophy.

YUTA's No vote on the Cardano Summit 2026 is the clearest example of accountability-based governance—citing the specific KPI from the 2025 proposal (15-20% developer growth) that was not met, and rejecting the 2026 proposal partly on that basis. This represents a sophisticated governance norm: prior commitments should be evaluated before new requests are approved.

Multiple DReps criticize gov.tools specifically: GAIA notes it's broken (governance dashboard doesn't display voting history, unresponsive support), Kostas Panagias notes inaccurate statistics. Several note the 500-character limit forced truncation of rationales. These are systemic issues affecting governance quality that are consistently raised across multiple DReps.

Several DReps invoke 'liquid democracy' as justification for supporting imperfect proposals (Kostas Panagias, HOSKY, Cerkoryn): 'we can always amend.' However, GAIA and InputEndorsers provide the counter-argument: governance capture and ADA price damage are not easily reversed. The tension between 'live governance' pragmatism and 'get it right' perfectionism is the defining debate of early Voltaire governance.

metadata.notes: Analysis based on rationale files as stored in the civitas rationale repository. Some DReps (TriangleForces, CardanoYoda) link to external files for full rationale; their in-file text was used as primary source. Some DRep files were absent from specific proposals, limiting cross-proposal comparison for those individuals.
